findings.exploit: Compromised upstream action could inject malicious code into CI pipeline.
findings.fix: Pin action to a specific commit SHA: uses: actions/checkout@<sha>

findings.title: RLS policy with CHECK (true) — unrestricted write
findings.description: RLS policy allows any authenticated user to write without restriction.
findings.exploit: Any user can insert/update records for any other user.
findings.fix: Replace WITH CHECK (true) with proper user-scoped check: WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id).

findings.title: RLS policy with CHECK (true) — unrestricted write

findings.fix: Replace WITH CHECK (true) with proper user-scoped check: WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id).

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER function without auth.uid() check: public.get_profile_by_email(p_email
findings.description: Function public.get_profile_by_email(p_email runs with elevated privileges but doesn't verify the caller's identity.
findings.exploit: Any authenticated user can invoke this function regardless of their role/relationship.
findings.fix: Add auth.uid() verification at the start of the function body.

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER function without auth.uid() check: public.get_all_tenants()
findings.description: Function public.get_all_tenants() runs with elevated privileges but doesn't verify the caller's identity.
findings.exploit: Any authenticated user can invoke this function regardless of their role/relationship.
findings.fix: Add auth.uid() verification at the start of the function body.

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER without search_path
findings.description: A SECURITY DEFINER function without explicit search_path is vulnerable to search_path hijacking.
findings.exploit: An attacker can create malicious objects in a schema that precedes 'public' in the search_path.
findings.fix: Add 'SET search_path = public, pg_catalog' to the function definition.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: No CSP header configured in Next.js config.
findings.exploit: Enables XSS attacks, data exfiltration, and clickjacking.
findings.fix: Add CSP header via next.config headers() function.

findings.title: X-Powered-By header not disabled
findings.description: Next.js exposes 'X-Powered-By: Next.js' header by default.
findings.exploit: Reveals technology stack, enabling targeted attacks.
findings.fix: Set poweredByHeader: false in next.config.

findings.title: Potential IDOR: delete/update without ownership check
findings.description: Database operation filtered only by resource ID without user ownership verification.
findings.exploit: An attacker can modify the ID parameter to access/modify other users' resources.
findings.fix: Add .eq('owner_id', user.id) or .eq('user_id', user.id) to the query.
